instruction: Highlight the cell representing the first day of every month in the calendar spreadsheet with a green (#00ff00) background; do not alter any other cells.

metadata.explanation: Task requires highlighting the first day of each month (5 cells total: June 1, July 1, August 1, September 1, October 1) in green. Verified with Python: identified 5 cells where date.day == 1. Custom getter extracts background colors from first-day cells, custom metric compares against expected green color with tolerance.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator correctly verifies BOTH requirements - (1) expected first-day cells ARE green, AND (2) ONLY those cells are green
Correct negative verification: Metric Check 3 (lines 73-77) verifies that NO non-first-day cells have green highlights, returning 0.0 if violation found
Correct exclusivity check: Metric Check 2 (lines 65-71) verifies that NO extra first-day cells beyond the expected list are highlighted green, penalizing with 0.5 score
Proper data flow: Getter extracts both first_day_colors and non_first_day_colors, metric validates all three conditions (expected present, no extra first-days, no non-first-days)
Robust edge case handling: colors_match function properly handles None values, alpha channels, and color tolerance with Euclidean distance
Semantically correct expected values: 5 cells (B3-F3) represent the 5 first-days-of-month in a calendar, with correct green color #00FF00
